chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, who said:
I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the fermented drink, so he wrote forbidding me from it.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan, referring to Imam Al-Hasan ibn Ali (AS), the second or eleventh Imam depending on the count, here identified by his kunya.
key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: A specific type of fermented drink, often identified as a weak beer or fermented grain beverage, mentioned in hadiths regarding intoxicants.
key_terms.يَنْهَانِي: He forbade me; indicates a prohibition (kahr) rather than mere dislike (karahah).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Fuqqa' according to Imam Al-Hasan (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records a direct inquiry from Ibn Fazzal to Imam Al-Hasan (AS) regarding 'al-fuqqa'', a specific fermented drink, to which the Imam responded with a prohibition. This ruling establishes the beverage as 'kahr' (forbidden), serving as a foundational precedent in Shia jurisprudence for classifying fermented intoxicants based on their production method and effect. The transmission chain highlights the scholarly rigor of the early Imams in addressing specific contemporary dietary practices.
